A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AFFMAE and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. Inspection includes v2's supplementary Section 7; v1 ends after its references. The substantial revisions can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original FPW segmentation, computational-efficiency measurements, component ablations, and training-data-efficiency experiments.

after.justification: V2 reports original FPW comparisons, component and decoder experiments, and evaluations on three public electron-microscopy benchmarks.

M1.justification: V2 introduces cached, quantized-grid KNN retrieval in place of separate neighbor searches for decoder queries (Sections 3.3 and 7.1). This is a localized procedural change to the retained framework of adaptive merging, stable interpolation, Perlin masking, and deep supervision.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluations on Lucchi++, Kasthuri++, and the 2012 ISBI EM Challenge, substantially broadening microscopy coverage beyond FPW. The reported FPW segmentation task also narrows from four foreground classes to the basement-membrane interface and filtration slits, retaining background.

E2.justification: The FPW comparison expands from ViT-MAE in v1 Table 1 to include SimMIM, MixMAE, GreenMIM, HiViT, and nnU-Net V2 in v2 Table 2. These are evaluated comparators, whereas several appeared only as related work in v1.

E3.justification: Reported main models increase from approximately 22M to 65M parameters, with pretraining/fine-tuning schedules changing from 300/700 to 400/400 epochs. FPW test size changes from 164 to 235, and resolutions from 448/512/768 to 512/768/1024. V2 also introduces CLAHE preprocessing, UperNet baseline heads, Slits IoU and FPW-error metrics, revised memory-measurement batch sizes, and public-benchmark protocols.

E4.justification: V2 adds controls for initialization source, deepest-stage-only reconstruction, ViT with the point decoder, and cached versus standard decoder execution. It removes v1's training-data-fraction study (Figure 11) and the 65% masking-ratio ablation entry. Existing representation-collapse and spectral analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V2 Table 2 first reports main FPW scores as mean ± standard deviation across four random seeds. Table 4 additionally reports timing variation over 30 trials. V1 provides point estimates without corresponding model-run or uncertainty information; an increase from a known v1 run count cannot be established.

E6.justification: Main and ablation results are extensively replaced: AFFMAE's 512-pixel mIoU is 0.6030 in v1 Table 1 versus 0.608 ± 0.002 in v2 Table 2 under revised settings, not a same-setting gain. V2 adds FPW errors, decoder timings, and public-benchmark results, including AFFMAE mIoUs of 0.8829, 0.8870, and 0.8661 in Table 6.

T1.justification: V2 adds limited complexity arguments: cached KNN retrieval is effectively O(1) per query after table construction, and the volumetric discussion derives O(n^6) versus O(n^4) dense-attention scaling. Core interpolation and normalized-effective-rank mathematics remain equivalent; no theorem or proof framework is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains efficient, mask-agnostic hierarchical pretraining with ViT-level microscopy segmentation. V2 refines the headline contributions toward reusable segmentation decoding, 2× pretraining and 5× fine-tuning speedups, and better slit segmentation than grid-based hierarchies, replacing v1's emphasis on up to 7× FLOP reduction.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive discussion of token-location interpretability, volumetric applicability, and bandwidth/cache limitations that can erode efficiency at very high resolutions. It also replaces v1's interpretation of robustness at 75% masking with an account of noticeable degradation and explains the failure of deepest-stage-only reconstruction.

D1.justification: Supplementary Sections 7.1–7.7 add architecture configurations, cached-neighbor implementation details, preprocessing parameters, segmentation-head adaptation, benchmark-specific optimization settings, and measured pretraining hours. Hardware disclosure also expands to identify H100-trained baselines, although this conflicts with the main text's blanket RTX 5090 description.

R1.justification: Research positioning substantially shifts toward kidney ultrastructure and comparisons with sparse hierarchical masked-modeling approaches. V2 adds GreenMIM, HiViT, clinical FPW, public-benchmark, and segmentation-decoder references while removing the separate adaptive-token survey covering DynamicViT, A-ViT, and AdaViT. The earlier broad criticism of competing hierarchical methods is rewritten.

P1.justification: The title, introduction, related work, method explanations, and results narrative are extensively rewritten. Method subsections are reorganized, ablations precede main results, and dedicated discussion/limitations and supplementary sections replace the earlier compact structure.

P2.justification: V2 switches to a single-column layout, merges existing collapse and masking figures, redesigns efficiency displays, and substantially expands comparison-table structure. New architecture/cache diagrams and qualitative panels are added, while v1's data-efficiency plot is removed. These are substantive display changes beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially remedies v1's narrow validation through additional FPW baselines, three public EM benchmarks, four-seed reporting, and fuller implementation and limitation disclosures. These strengthen evidential breadth and reproducibility. The removed low-data study, inconsistent GPU descriptions, and SimMIM prose/table discrepancy are drawbacks; revised FPW settings also prevent direct version-to-version performance claims. They do not outweigh the stronger support for the central accuracy-efficiency contribution.
